title: Real Clifford Modules, KO Theory, and ABS Orientations

items.title: Real and quaternionic bundle K-groups
items.statement:
For a compact Hausdorff space $X$, let $KO^0(X)$ be the group completion of the direct-sum monoid of finite-rank real vector bundles, and let $KSp^0(X)$ be the corresponding group for finite-rank right-$\mathbb H$ bundles and right-$\mathbb H$-linear maps. Ranks may vary between connected components. In particular these definitions apply to finite CW complexes. A group-completion element is $[E]-[F]$; equality means that a bundle $G$ exists with $E\oplus F'\oplus G\cong E'\oplus F\oplus G$ for the two differences concerned.

Pullback defines contravariant maps. Real tensor product makes $KO^0(X)$ a commutative ring with unit $[\mathbb R]$. Tensoring a real bundle with a right-$\mathbb H$ bundle over $\mathbb R$ gives a $KO^0(X)$-module structure on $KSp^0(X)$. No internal quaternionic tensor product is asserted.

items.title: Given Spin and Spin-c structures and their spinor bundles
items.statement: Let V→X be an oriented Euclidean real vector bundle of rank n, with oriented frame bundle P_SO(V). Use Spin(n)=Spin_N=1(ℝⁿ,−‖·‖²), the norm-one even subgroup of the negative-square Clifford algebra, and its standard twisted-Clifford homomorphism λ_n:Spin(n)→SO(n). A Spin structure on V is a principal Spin(n)-bundle P with a Spin(n)-equivariant two-fold map P→P_SO(V) covering the identity on X and compatible with λ_n. A Spin^c structure is a principal Spin^c(n) lift of P_SO(V), where Spin^c(n)=(Spin(n)×U(1))/⟨(−1,−1)⟩. A spinor bundle is the associated bundle for the specified real Clifford representation; a Spin^c spinor bundle uses the specified complex representation and its U(1) weight. These are given structures; this definition asserts no existence criterion.

items.title: Real graded Clifford-module bundles and their Grothendieck groups
items.statement:
Let $V\to X$ be a finite-rank Euclidean real vector bundle and put $C(V)=\mathrm{Cl}(V,-\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$, so each vector $v$ acts with square $-\lVert v\rVert^2$. An **ungraded** $C(V)$-module bundle is a finite-rank real vector bundle with continuous fiberwise unital Clifford action. Write $K_{C(V)}(X)$ for the Grothendieck group of their direct-sum monoid.

A **graded** $C(V)$-module bundle is a module $\Lambda=\Lambda^0\oplus\Lambda^1$ whose action satisfies $C(V)^i\Lambda^j\subseteq\Lambda^{i+j}$, with indices modulo two. In particular vector multiplication is odd: it exchanges the two parity subbundles. Write $M(V)$ for the Grothendieck group of graded modules. The same convention gives $M_n$ for the negative Clifford algebra $C_n=\mathrm{Cl}_{0,n}$ over a point. Ungraded $K_{C(V)}(X)$ and graded $M(V)$ are distinct groups; neither is identified with the other by notation. The rank-$4m$ volume Thom theorem uses the former, whereas ABS uses a restriction quotient of the latter.

items.title: A numerated real bundle embeds in a finite trivial bundle
items.statement: Let $X$ be compact Hausdorff and let $E\to X$ be a rank-$r$ real vector bundle with a finite linear trivializing cover $(U_i,\tau_i)$ and a subordinate finite partition of unity $(\rho_i)$. Then some $N$ and a bundle $F\to X$ satisfy $E\oplus F\cong X\times\mathbb R^N$. The embedding and orthogonal complement construction uses only the supplied finite numeration.

items.title: Orthogonal Clifford families and centriole spaces
items.statement: Let p be a positive even integer and define SO(p)={J∈M_p(ℝ):JᵀJ=I, det J=1}. Its trace metric is the left-invariant Riemannian metric whose inner product at the identity is ⟨A,B⟩=−(1/p)tr(AB) for skew-symmetric A,B; at J its value on tangent vectors JA,JB is the same. An orthogonal negative-square Clifford family of length l is a list J₁,…,J_l∈SO(p) with J_i²=−I and J_iJ_j=−J_jJ_i for i≠j, equivalently a representation of C_l=Cl(ℝ^l,−‖·‖²) by these matrices. For a Riemannian manifold P and points x,y, its midpoint set is {γ(1/2): γ:[0,1]→P is a length-minimizing geodesic from x to y}; a centriole is a connected component of such a midpoint set. Put P₀=SO(p), J₀=I, and for j≥1 define P̂_j={J∈SO(p):J²=−I and JJ_i=−J_iJ for i<j}; let P_j be the connected component of P̂_j containing J_j. A compatible family also satisfies J_j∈P_(j−1). The geometric midpoint interpretation of this algebraic component is the claim of the next lemma.

items.title: Finite-dimensional gapped free Hamiltonians and stable equivalence
items.statement:
A finite-dimensional free-fermion Hamiltonian is a self-adjoint matrix on a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. It is gapped at zero if 0 is not in its spectrum. A symmetry class is specified by named unitary and antiunitary operators and exact commutation, anticommutation and square relations with H. Stable equivalence means gap-preserving homotopy after direct sum with fixed reference trivial bands; phases are differences of stabilized systems, not absolute modules.

Class A has no additional antiunitary constraint. A symmetry is unitary or antiunitary and its relation is recorded as S H S^{-1}=σH, σ∈{+1,−1}; any additional square relation is part of the declared model data.

items.title: Relative Morse–Bott crossing by negative normal disk bundles
items.statement: Assume AC. Let a smooth function have a compact band whose critical locus is a finite union of compact embedded critical manifolds, with Hessian kernel exactly the tangent space of each. Crossing one component attaches its negative normal disk bundle, with its positive normal disk thickening. If every nonminimum negative normal rank exceeds $d$, finite-CW parameter maps of dimension at most $d$ can be moved relatively past those components. A sufficiently small neighborhood of a clean minimum retracts onto that minimum manifold.

items.title: Stabilized upper gauge cancellation by block rotation
items.statement: Let two sphere-bundle clutching triples have the same upper bundle $F$, and let $\phi$ be an orthogonal bundle isomorphism between their glued bundles. After adding the pulled-back bundle $\pi^*F$ to both triples, there is an orthogonal isomorphism with upper gauge equal to the identity. The target clutching map can be kept literally fixed.

items.title: Reduced and relative real K-theory and compact support
items.statement:
For a based compact Hausdorff space $(Y,*)$, set $\widetilde {KO}^0(Y)=\ker(KO^0(Y)\to KO^0(*))$. For a compact pair with closed subspace $A\subset X$, set $KO^0(X,A)=\widetilde {KO}^0(X/A)$, where all of $A$ is collapsed to one basepoint. If $A=\varnothing$, use $X_+=X\amalg\{*\}$ instead. Set $KO^{-j}(X,A)=\widetilde {KO}^0(S^j\wedge(X/A))$ for $j\geq0$, and $KO^{-j}(X)=KO^{-j}(X,\varnothing)$. The same conventions define reduced, relative and negative-degree $KSp$.

For a finite-rank metric real bundle $V\to X$ over compact $X$, write $\operatorname{Th}(V)=D(V)/S(V)$ and $KO_c^{-j}(V)=\widetilde {KO}^0(S^j\wedge\operatorname{Th}(V))$. At rank zero use $\operatorname{Th}(0)=X_+$. These definitions do not assert any periodicity or an isomorphism between successive degrees.

items.title: Clifford-module restriction cokernels A_n
items.statement: For n≥0 put C_n=Cl(ℝ^n,−‖·‖²). Let M_n be the Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional real Z/2-graded left C_n-modules and let r_n:M_{n+1}→M_n be restriction along the standard inclusion of the first n Clifford generators. Define A_n=coker(r_n). For n=0 the grading is retained, so M_0≅Z⊕Z from even and odd dimensions; no parity type is identified with a volume-element eigenspace.

items.title: Finite-CW real bundles have orthogonal complements under AC
items.statement: Assume AC. If $X$ is a finite CW complex and $E\to X$ is any finite-rank real vector bundle, then $E$ is isomorphic to a subbundle of a finite trivial bundle and has an orthogonal vector-bundle complement.

items.title: Clifford centrioles and geodesic tangent conditions
items.statement: Assume AC and let $p\ge2$ be even. For an orthogonal negative-square Clifford family $J_1,\ldots,J_l$ on $\mathbb R^p$, use the metric $\langle A,B\rangle=-p^{-1}\operatorname{tr}(AB)$ on $\mathfrak{so}(p)$ and the component $P_j$ of $\widehat P_j$ containing $J_j$. The midpoint component through $J_j$ in $P_{j-1}$ is exactly $P_j$. Each $P_j$ is a compact totally geodesic symmetric submanifold. For $A\in\mathfrak{so}(p)$, the curve $\exp(tA)J_j$ stays in $P_j$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$ if and only if $AJ_j=-J_jA$ and $AJ_i=J_iA$ for $i<j$. Successive midpoint assertions require the indicated antipodes to lie in the same component; no unconditional extendibility is asserted.

items.title: Volume chirality and Clifford–Hopf clutching
items.statement: Let $V\to X$ be an oriented Euclidean real vector bundle of rank $n=4m>0$ and let $\Lambda$ be a real ungraded $C(V)$-module bundle, where $C(V)=\mathrm{Cl}(V,-\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$. In an oriented orthonormal frame $(e_1,\ldots,e_n)$ set $\omega=c(e_1)\cdots c(e_n)$. Then $\omega$ is frame-independent, has square $1$, and its eigenspaces $\Lambda^+$ and $\Lambda^-$ are subbundles interchanged by multiplication by every unit vector $v$. Gluing the pullbacks of $\Lambda^+$ and $\Lambda^-$ over the two disk halves of $S(\mathbb R\oplus V)$ by $c(v):\Lambda^+\to\Lambda^-$ along $S(V)$ defines the associated Clifford–Hopf clutching bundle. If $\Lambda$ is additionally a graded module, $\omega$ preserves its parity and the eigenbundles are graded. Its relative clutching triple is $(\Lambda^+,c(v),\Lambda^-)$; the volume eigensplitting is distinct from both the module parity grading and the canonical word-length grading $C(V)=C(V)^0\oplus C(V)^1$ on the regular algebra.

items.title: Complex Spin-c Thom orientation from the equivariant spinor symbol
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $V\to X$ have even rank $2l$ and a given Spin-c structure
over a finite CW pair $(X,A)$. Its complex spinor symbol defines
$\tau_V^c\in\widetilde K^0(\operatorname{Th}(V))$ and natural isomorphisms

$$K^j(X,A)\xrightarrow{\cong}\widetilde K^j(\operatorname{Th}(V)/\operatorname{Th}(V|_A)),\qquad a\longmapsto\pi^*a\,\tau_V^c$$

for every integer $j$. The map is multiplicative under the direct-sum
Spin-c structure. The complex theory and its Bott theorem are used only
in this complex assertion.

items.title: Spectral flattening preserves gaps and symmetry relations
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional self-adjoint gapped Hamiltonian $H$, define $\operatorname{sign}(H)$ by its spectral decomposition: it is $+1$ on positive eigenspaces and $-1$ on negative eigenspaces. The path $H_t=(1-t)H+t\operatorname{sign}(H)$ is continuous, remains gapped, and preserves every unitary or antiunitary symmetry relation $S H S^{-1}=\sigma H$ with $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$. At $t=1$ it is a self-adjoint involution.

items.title: Finite-CW relative KO triples and homotopy invariance
items.statement: Assume AC. For a finite CW pair $(X,A)$, $KO^0(X,A)$ is naturally the group of triples $(E,F,g)$, with $E,F$ real bundles on $X$ and $g:E|_A\to F|_A$ an isomorphism. Relations are bundle isomorphism, direct-sum additivity, homotopy of $g$, and deletion of a triple whose $g$ extends to an isomorphism on $X$. Equivalently, use stable homotopy of triples, allowing addition of such elementary triples. Pullback along homotopic maps of pairs induces equal maps. In degree zero over $X$, equality of virtual bundles is equality after common trivial stabilization. Every real bundle on $X$ has a finite trivial complement. The analogous complement, stable-isomorphism, homotopy and triple statements hold for right-$\mathbb H$ bundles. All these conclusions also hold for compact Hausdorff pairs with closed subspace; this includes disk, sphere and Thom bundle spaces over compact finite CW bases.

items.title: Real Clifford block-rotation index bounds
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $\gamma$ be a nonminimizing endpoint-fixed geodesic from $J_l$ to $-J_l$ in a Clifford centriole $P_l$, with the normalized trace metric. Let $s_j$ be the real dimension of an irreducible negative-square Clifford module. If $l\not\equiv2\pmod4$, then $\operatorname{ind}\gamma\ge p/s_{l+1}-1$. If $l=4m-2$, let $w$ be determinant winding under $J\mapsto JJ_l^{-1}$ into $\mathrm U(p/2)$. For $d>0$, the inequality $p-4|w|\ge4d s_l$ implies $\operatorname{ind}\gamma>d$. The first estimate is non-strict; its use for connectivity requires additional strict slack.

items.title: Ungraded real and quaternionic spinor Morita evaluation
items.statement:
Assume AC and let $V\to X$ be a given Spin Euclidean bundle over a finite CW
complex, of positive rank $8m$ or $8m+4$. Let $\Sigma$ be the associated
irreducible **ungraded** real $C(V)$-module bundle; it acquires its canonical
volume grading but arbitrary independent gradings are not part of this
category. In rank $8m$ evaluation gives an equivalence between real bundles
and ungraded $C(V)$-module bundles. In rank $8m+4$ it gives an equivalence
between right-$\mathbb H$ bundles and ungraded $C(V)$-module bundles, by

$$E\longmapsto E\otimes_{\mathbb H}\Sigma,\qquad \Lambda\longmapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{C(V)}(\Sigma,\Lambda).$$

Here $\Sigma$ has its commuting right action $s\mapsto sq$; its left action
for balancing is $q\cdot s=s\bar q$, and the Hom right action is
$(f\cdot q)(s)=f(s\bar q)$. Evaluation $f\otimes s\mapsto f(s)$ is an
isomorphism. The equivalences are natural, additive and induce
$KO^0(X)\cong K_{C(V)}(X)$ and $KSp^0(X)\cong K_{C(V)}(X)$ respectively.

items.title: The ABS Clifford cokernel and symbol map
items.statement:
For C_n=Cl(ℝ^n,−‖·‖²), a finite-dimensional graded real module M=M^0⊕M^1 determines the ABS symbol triple (π^*M^0,π^*M^1,c(v)) on the disk/sphere pair of ℝ^n: over a nonzero vector v, Clifford multiplication c(v) is an isomorphism because c(v)^2=−‖v‖²I. Its relative KO class is the candidate symbol. The separate theorem proves that the symbol vanishes on restrictions from C_(n+1), descends to A_n, and is an isomorphism.

The symbol is a relative class on the disk/sphere pair; since c(v) is invertible for v≠0, the triple is admissible. This definition alone does not claim factorization through A_n.

items.title: Graded C_n modules and ungraded C_(n−1) modules
items.statement: For $n\ge1$, taking the even part is an equivalence from finite-dimensional graded $C_n$-modules to finite-dimensional ungraded $C_{n-1}$-modules, where $C_n=\mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb R^n,-\lVert\cdot\rVert^2)$. An inverse is induction from the even subalgebra. For $n=0$, retain both parity types and treat the restriction cokernel separately.

items.title: Antiunitary AZ symmetry classes give Clifford extension problems
items.statement: In the finite-dimensional stable gapped free model, use the normalized AZ relation algebra: antiunitaries $T,C$ have $T^2=t$, $C^2=c$, with $t,c\in\{1,-1\}$, $TH=HT$, $CH=-HC$, and $TC=CT$ when both are present. A lone chiral symmetry is a self-adjoint unitary involution anticommuting with $H$. The real extension indices are $\mathrm{AI},\mathrm{BDI},\mathrm D,\mathrm{DIII},\mathrm{AII},\mathrm{CII},\mathrm C,\mathrm{CI}$ at $q=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7$, respectively. The complex classes A and AIII have indices $0,1$ modulo two. They are obtained by the explicit realification and mass generators below. Adding $d$ fixed negative-square Dirac generators decreases the real index to $q-d$. Individual $T,C$ squares without the specified mutual relation do not define this normalized tenfold algebra; additional unitary symmetries remain extra model data.

items.title: Clean energy critical manifolds in Clifford-centriole polygon spaces
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $P$ be $\mathrm{SO}(p)$ or a Clifford centriole $P_l$ with the normalized trace metric, and let $(o,q)$ be its indicated pole pair $(I,-I)$ or $(J_l,-J_l)$ in one component. For a fixed energy bound $c$, choose a convexity radius $r>0$ and a mesh $n$ with $c/n<r^2$. The short-edge polygon energy has compact sublevels in each path component. Its critical points are precisely sampled smooth constant-speed geodesics. Its Hessian has the same index and kernel as the path index form. The critical loci in a bounded sublevel form a finite union of compact Morse–Bott manifolds, with Hessian kernel equal to the tangent to the endpoint-fixing isotropy orbit.

items.title: Suspension, exactness, and products in relative KO
items.statement:
Assume AC. Finite CW pairs have the natural cofiber exact sequence

$$\cdots\longrightarrow KO^{-j-1}(X)\longrightarrow KO^{-j-1}(A)\xrightarrow{\partial}KO^{-j}(X,A)\longrightarrow KO^{-j}(X)\longrightarrow KO^{-j}(A)\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow KO^0(A).$$

This sequence continues indefinitely to the left; a positive-degree continuation requires a separately proved periodicity theorem. The reduced suspension identity is $\widetilde {KO}^{-j}(\Sigma Y)=\widetilde {KO}^{-j-1}(Y)$. There are natural associative products

$$KO^{-p}(X,A)\otimes KO^{-q}(Y,B)\longrightarrow KO^{-p-q}(X\times Y,A\times Y\cup X\times B),$$

which in absolute degree zero are the bundle tensor product. They commute with the suspension identifications with the order of sphere coordinates retained, and interchange of degrees $-p,-q$ has sign $(-1)^{pq}$. The diagonal gives internal products; a real factor acts on relative $KSp$. For a metric bundle $V$, the quotient $\widehat V/s_+(X)$, where $\widehat V=S(\mathbb R\oplus V)$, is naturally homeomorphic to $\operatorname{Th}(V)$. At rank zero both are $X_+$. The reduced groups split $KO^0(Y)=\widetilde {KO}^0(Y)\oplus\mathbb Z$ at a chosen basepoint. The analogous exactness and suspension statements hold for $KSp$.

items.title: Relative path-shortening connectivity from index bounds
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $P$ be $\mathrm{SO}(p)$ or a Clifford centriole with normalized trace metric and indicated antipodal pole pair in one component. In a fixed endpoint-path component suppose every geodesic which is not energy-minimizing in that component has index at least $d+1$. Then the inclusion of constant-speed minimizing geodesics into the $H^1$ path space, and into the continuous compact-open path space, is $d$-connected: every map of a finite CW pair $(K,A)$ with $\dim K\le d$, taking $A$ to the minima, deforms relative to $A$ into the minima.

items.title: Real and symplectic clutching groups in low degrees
items.statement:
Assume AC. Clutching and stabilization give natural additive identifications, for $n\geq1$,

$$\widetilde {KO}^0(S^n)\cong\underset r{\operatorname{colim}}\,\pi_{n-1}(O(r)),\qquad\widetilde {KSp}^0(S^n)\cong\underset r{\operatorname{colim}}\,\pi_{n-1}(Sp(r)).$$

At $n=1$ the right sides mean component groups under block sum. Then $KO^0(*)=KSp^0(*)=\mathbb Z$ by real and quaternionic dimension, respectively, and

$$KO^{-1}(*)=\mathbb Z/2,\qquad KO^{-2}(*)=\mathbb Z/2,\qquad KO^{-3}(*)=0,$$

$$KSp^{-1}(*)=KSp^{-2}(*)=KSp^{-3}(*)=0.$$

Here $Sp(r)$ is the compact group of right-$\mathbb H$-linear isometries of $\mathbb H^r$. These calculations use no Bott periodicity or KO coefficient table.

items.title: Restriction matrices for negative-square graded real Clifford modules
items.statement:
Use $C_n=\mathrm{Cl}_{0,n}$ and the graded groups $M_n$ and restriction maps
$r_n:M_{n+1}\to M_n$. In the irreducible bases specified below the matrices are

| $n$ | $M_n$ | $M_{n+1}$ | $r_n$ | $A_n$ |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| $0$ | $\mathbb Z^2$ | $\mathbb Z$ | $\binom11$ | $\mathbb Z$ |
| $1$ | $\mathbb Z$ | $\mathbb Z$ | $(2)$ | $\mathbb Z/2$ |
| $2$ | $\mathbb Z$ | $\mathbb Z$ | $(2)$ | $\mathbb Z/2$ |
| $3$ | $\mathbb Z$ | $\mathbb Z^2$ | $(1\ \ 1)$ | $0$ |
| $4$ | $\mathbb Z^2$ | $\mathbb Z$ | $\binom11$ | $\mathbb Z$ |
| $5$ | $\mathbb Z$ | $\mathbb Z$ | $(1)$ | $0$ |
| $6$ | $\mathbb Z$ | $\mathbb Z$ | $(1)$ | $0$ |
| $7$ | $\mathbb Z$ | $\mathbb Z^2$ | $(1\ \ 1)$ | $0$ |

The table continues with period eight by tensoring with a chosen irreducible
graded $C_8$-module $B$. The generator of a split-row cokernel is the first
irreducible modulo the diagonal, with the second its negative. At $n=0$ this
is the even-minus-odd rank convention.

items.title: Iterated suspension and winding control
items.statement:
Assume AC. Fix $k=4m-1$ and a positive orthogonal $C_k$ representation on $\mathbb R^p$, meaning $J_k=J_1\cdots J_{k-1}$. Fixed-meridian geodesic suspension defines a composite
$$\theta:\operatorname{Map}_*(S^1,P_{k-1})\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_*(S^k,\mathrm{SO}(p)).$$
It is $d$-connected when $p$ satisfies the finite size inequalities below. Earlier extendible stages in residue $l=4a-2$ have winding zero. Terminal determinant winding defines a stable, additive label on based sphere maps, independent of positive representation, orthogonal gauge, and stabilization by constant blocks.

items.title: Affine Clifford–Hopf maps are highly connected
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $k=4m-1$, $d\ge1$, and let $\rho$ be a positive orthogonal $C_k$ representation on $\mathbb R^p$. Let $s_k$ be the irreducible real dimension. If $p\ge p_0(d,k)$ and $s_kd\le\eta\le p/4$, then the inclusion
$$\operatorname{Hopf}_\rho(S^k,\mathrm{SO}(p))_\eta\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_*(S^k,\mathrm{SO}(p))_\eta$$
is $d$-connected for finite CW pairs. Here the right-hand side is the union of mapping components of stable winding $\eta$. The left-hand side consists of $I$ on an invariant $L_0$ and $x_0I+\sum_{j=1}^kx_jJ_j$ on an invariant $L_1$, where $\mathbb R^p=L_0\oplus L_1$ and $\dim_{\mathbb C}L_1=\eta$ relative to $i=J_1\cdots J_{k-2}$.

items.title: Stable Clifford–Hopf decomposition over sphere bundles
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $X$ be a finite CW complex and $V\to X$ oriented Euclidean of rank $n=4m>0$. Put $\widehat V=S(\mathbb R\oplus V)$, with projection $\pi$ and pole sections $s_\pm$. For an ungraded $C(V)$-module bundle $\Lambda$, let $H(\Lambda)$ be the clutching bundle with upper and lower halves the volume eigenspaces $\Lambda^\pm$ and transition $c(v):\Lambda^+\to\Lambda^-$ along $S(V)$. Every real bundle on $\widehat V$ becomes $\pi^*E_0\oplus H(\Lambda)$ after addition of finitely many trivial real bundles and copies of $H(C(V))$, where the regular module uses volume chirality. The proof also gives relative extension of an affine splitting and its lower-disk gauge over any finite CW subcomplex, in the dimension-dependent range stated below.

items.title: Uniqueness of the stable Clifford–Hopf decomposition
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $X$ be finite CW and $V\to X$ oriented Euclidean of rank $4m>0$. Suppose $\pi^*E_0\oplus H(\Lambda)$ and $\pi^*E_1\oplus H(M)$ become isomorphic after adding the same trivial real and regular Clifford–Hopf summands. Then $E_0,E_1$ are ordinarily stably isomorphic, and the ungraded $C(V)$-modules $\Lambda,M$ become isomorphic after adding equal regular module summands. The proof uses relative affine decomposition over $X\times I$ in dimension $\dim X+1$.

items.title: Real Clifford–Thom isomorphism
items.statement:
Assume AC. For $X$ finite CW and $V\to X$ oriented Euclidean of positive rank $n=4m$, let $K_{C(V)}(X)$ be the Grothendieck group of ungraded real $C(V)$-module bundles. Then
$$\Psi_V:K_{C(V)}(X)\longrightarrow\widetilde{KO}^0(\operatorname{Th}(V)),\qquad [\Lambda]\longmapsto[H(\Lambda)]-\pi^*[\Lambda^+]$$
is an isomorphism, where the last expression is identified with the kernel of restriction to the north section. The decomposition map $T:KO^0(X)\oplus K_{C(V)}(X)\to KO^0(\widehat V)$ has zero kernel, and $\ker(\chi T)=KO^0(X)\oplus\{0\}$ for $\chi(z)=z-\pi^*s_+^*z$. With the standard ABS relative-triple sign, the volume-positive symbol is $\Phi_V=-\Psi_V$, also an isomorphism. Rank zero is separately the identity $KO^0(X)\cong\widetilde{KO}^0(X_+)$.

items.title: Real Spin Thom isomorphisms with real and quaternionic sources
items.statement:
Assume AC. For a given Spin bundle $V\to X$ of positive rank $8m$, the
volume-graded irreducible real spinor symbol $\tau_V$ induces a natural
isomorphism $KO^0(X)\to KO_c^0(V)$ by $a\mapsto\pi^*a\,\tau_V$.
For rank $8m+4$ the natural isomorphism is
$KSp^0(X)\to KO_c^0(V)$, $[E]\mapsto\Phi_V(E\otimes_{\mathbb H}\Sigma)$,
using the balanced convention in the Morita lemma. The latter formula is
not ordinary product of two real KO classes. For rank zero, the canonical framed Spin lift gives the identity; an arbitrary given lift gives tensoring by its associated real line $L$, with $L^{\otimes2}\cong\mathbb R$.
The real branch is compatible with direct sums and products of spinor
symbols; mixed quaternionic branches use their balanced spinor tensors.

items.title: Real Bott periodicity from the rank-eight Clifford–Thom map
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $\beta\in\widetilde{KO}^0(S^8)=KO^{-8}(\mathrm{pt})$ be the volume-positive rank-eight real spinor symbol of the trivial bundle, with the source-minus-target relative-triple convention. For every finite CW pair $(X,A)$, multiplication by this same class is a natural isomorphism $KO^j(X,A)\to KO^{j-8}(X,A)$ in every integer degree. In particular it gives $KO^0(X)\cong\widetilde{KO}^0(X_+\wedge S^8)$. These maps respect external products; positive degrees are defined by the resulting periodic continuation of the bundle theory. No complexification or coefficient table is used.

items.title: The real KO coefficient table and eightfold periodicity
items.statement: Assume AC. For $n=0,\ldots,7$, the groups $KO^{-n}(\mathrm{pt})$ are respectively $\mathbb Z,\mathbb Z/2,\mathbb Z/2,0,\mathbb Z,0,0,0$. Multiplication by the volume-positive rank-eight spinor class $\beta$ gives $KO^j(\mathrm{pt})\cong KO^{j-8}(\mathrm{pt})$ for every integer $j$. The degree-four integer generator is the rank-four quaternionic spinor image of the quaternionic line; the degree-eight generator is the actual symbol $\beta$.

items.title: The actual ABS symbol identifies graded Clifford cokernels with KO
items.statement:
Assume AC. For $M=M^0\oplus M^1$ a graded real $C_n=\mathrm{Cl}_{0,n}$
module, let $a_M(v)=c(v)|_{M^0}:M^0\to M^1$. Its disk/sphere triple
$(\pi^*M^0,\pi^*M^1,a_M)$ gives $s_n(M)\in\widetilde{KO}^0(S^n)$.
For $n=0$ this means the even-minus-odd virtual vector space on $S^0$.
Then

$$\ker s_n=\operatorname{im}(r_n),\qquad \alpha_n:A_n\xrightarrow{\cong}KO^{-n}(\mathrm{pt}).$$

The maps are multiplicative under the graded tensor product. The chosen
degree-eight algebraic generator maps to the same $\beta$ that supplies
real Bott periodicity; no ABS theorem assuming preexisting periodicity
is a premise.

items.title: Real Spin KO Thom orientation in all ranks and degrees
items.statement:
Assume AC. A given Spin bundle $V\to X$ of rank $r\ge0$ on a finite CW
pair $(X,A)$ has a natural shifted class
$u_V\in\widetilde{KO}^{r}(\operatorname{Th}(V))$. Multiplication gives

$$KO^j(X,A)\xrightarrow{\cong}\widetilde{KO}^{j+r}(\operatorname{Th}(V)/\operatorname{Th}(V|_A))$$

for every integer $j$. The class is normalized to the suspended unit on
each fiber, independent of stabilization, natural for pullback of given
Spin structures, and multiplicative for direct sums. In unshifted degree
zero the rank $8m+4$ real-valued theorem has source $KSp^0(X)$, as proved
separately; that assertion is not replaced by a rank-zero real spinor.

items.title: Positive Clifford mass differences give the actual KO classes
items.statement:
Assume AC. Fix $q\geq0$ positive symmetric orthogonal Clifford generators $e_1,\ldots,e_q$ on a finite-dimensional real inner-product space. A mass is a symmetric orthogonal involution anticommuting with these generators. A mass difference consists of masses $H,H_0$ on fixed representations $W,W_0$, together with a specified isometric identification $w:W_0\to W$ intertwining the fixed generators. Use direct sum, mass homotopy, simultaneous orthogonal change of coordinates, and addition or deletion of a common reference extension as the stable difference relations. Denote the resulting component difference group by $D_q$.

There is an explicit natural additive isomorphism

$$\Psi_q:D_q\longrightarrow KO^{-q}(\mathrm{pt}).$$

At $q=0$ it is the **negative-eigenspace** rank difference

$$\Psi_0(H,H_0,w)=\dim W_H^- -\dim(W_0)_{H_0}^-.$$

In positive degrees it is the negative of the hemisphere-clutching class constructed below. Thus a determinant reflection at $q=1$ gives the reduced Möbius class; an orientation-component change at $q=2$ gives the real complex-Hopf class; and a positive negative-rank difference at $q=4$ gives the chosen quaternionic Hopf generator. Under the explicit eightfold matrix stabilization $T$, with $w$ stabilized along with the masses,

$$\Psi_{q+8}(T\delta)=\Psi_q(\delta)\boxtimes\beta,$$

where $\beta$ is exactly the volume-graded $C_8$ symbol supplying real Bott periodicity. In particular the negative-rank generator $(-1,+1)$ at $q=0$ stabilizes to a class mapping to $+\beta$. This statement concerns the finite stable Clifford mass problem and has no disorder or interaction conclusion.

items.title: Tenfold real and complex Clifford-extension table
items.statement:
Assume AC. For the normalized finite-dimensional stable free Dirac-mass extension problem with $d\ge0$ fixed negative-square Dirac generators, the strong difference group at real symmetry index $q$ is $KO^{-(q-d)}(\mathrm{pt})$. The complex analogue at indices $q=0,1$ is $KU^{-(q-d)}(\mathrm{pt})$. With columns indexed by $d$ modulo eight, the real table is

| class ($q$) | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ | $6$ | $7$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AI ($0$) | $\mathbb Z$ | $0$ | $0$ | $0$ | $\mathbb Z$ | $0$ | $\mathbb Z/2$ | $\mathbb Z/2$ |
| BDI ($1$) | $\mathbb Z/2$ | $\mathbb Z$ | $0$ | $0$ | $0$ | $\mathbb Z$ | $0$ | $\mathbb Z/2$ |
| D ($2$) | $\mathbb Z/2$ | $\mathbb Z/2$ | $\mathbb Z$ | $0$ | $0$ | $0$ | $\mathbb Z$ | $0$ |
| DIII ($3$) | $0$ | $\mathbb Z/2$ | $\mathbb Z/2$ | $\mathbb Z$ | $0$ | $0$ | $0$ | $\mathbb Z$ |
| AII ($4$) | $\mathbb Z$ | $0$ | $\mathbb Z/2$ | $\mathbb Z/2$ | $\mathbb Z$ | $0$ | $0$ | $0$ |
| CII ($5$) | $0$ | $\mathbb Z$ | $0$ | $\mathbb Z/2$ | $\mathbb Z/2$ | $\mathbb Z$ | $0$ | $0$ |
| C ($6$) | $0$ | $0$ | $\mathbb Z$ | $0$ | $\mathbb Z/2$ | $\mathbb Z/2$ | $\mathbb Z$ | $0$ |
| CI ($7$) | $0$ | $0$ | $0$ | $\mathbb Z$ | $0$ | $\mathbb Z/2$ | $\mathbb Z/2$ | $\mathbb Z$ |

For the two complex rows, A is $\mathbb Z$ in even $d$ and zero in odd $d$; AIII is zero in even $d$ and $\mathbb Z$ in odd $d$. Integer units count negative real multiplicity rank at real index zero, negative quaternionic multiplicity rank at index four, and negative complex rank in class A. The result concerns only the specified stable free mass problem; it gives no weak lattice, arbitrary-disorder or interaction-stable classification.

title: Real Clifford Modules, KO Theory, and ABS Orientations: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Low-dimensional real Clifford signatures
items.statement: Write $\mathbb H$ for the real algebra with basis $1,i,j,k$, relations $i^2=j^2=k^2=ijk=-1$, and $ij=k$. Under the positive-square-first convention, the algebras $\mathrm{Cl}_{1,0}$, $\mathrm{Cl}_{0,1}$, $\mathrm{Cl}_{2,0}$, $\mathrm{Cl}_{1,1}$, and $\mathrm{Cl}_{0,2}$ are respectively $\mathbb R\oplus\mathbb R$, $\mathbb C$, $M_2(\mathbb R)$, $M_2(\mathbb R)$, and $\mathbb H$.

items.title: Changing the Clifford square sign changes the low-rank algebra
items.statement: The assertion that the one-generator real Clifford algebras for $v^2=+1$ and $v^2=-1$ are isomorphic is false: the former is $\mathbb R\oplus\mathbb R$ and the latter is $\mathbb C$.

items.title: The tangent bundle of RP² is not Spin
items.statement: A Spin structure can be supplied to every tangent bundle. In particular, the tangent bundle of $\mathbb{RP}^2$ would admit one.

items.title: A zero-dimensional class-A flattened Hamiltonian
items.statement: On $\mathbb C^2$, let $H=\operatorname{diag}(-1,+1)$. Define the $d=0$ rank-difference index by $\nu(H)=\dim E_{<0}(H)-\dim E_{<0}(H_{\rm ref})$, where $H_{\rm ref}$ is the fixed reference system; choose the zero-band reference, whose negative eigenspace has dimension zero. Then $H$ is already flattened, with occupied projection $P=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)$, and the example has $\nu(H)=1$.

items.title: The zero-dimensional Clifford cokernel is Z
items.statement: For $C_0=\mathbb R$ with the trivial grading, a finite-dimensional graded module is $M=M^0\oplus M^1$. Its Grothendieck group is $M_0\cong\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z$ by $(\dim M^0,\dim M^1)$. For $C_1=\mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb R,-\lVert\cdot\rVert^2)$ the odd generator $e$ satisfies $e^2=-1$ and identifies the even and odd components of every graded module. Conversely, for every $k\ge0$, $\mathbb R^k\oplus\mathbb R^k$ with $e(x,y)=(-y,x)$ is a graded $C_1$-module. Therefore the restriction image is the diagonal subgroup and $A_0\cong\mathbb Z$ by even dimension minus odd dimension.

items.title: Rank four mod eight has KSp as the unshifted source
items.statement: Assume AC. For a given Spin bundle of rank $8m+4$, the source of the unshifted real Thom map is $KSp^0(X)$. The real spinor is quaternionic, so the rank-eight $KO^0(X)$ statement cannot be substituted in this residue class.

items.title: The low-degree real KO coefficient table
items.statement: Assume AC. The coefficients $KO^{-n}(\mathrm{pt})$ in residues $n=0,\ldots,7$ are $\mathbb Z,\mathbb Z/2,\mathbb Z/2,0,\mathbb Z,0,0,0$. The degree-four integer generator is quaternionic spinor clutching, and degree eight is generated by the fixed real Bott symbol $\beta$.

items.title: A one-dimensional BDI Dirac-mass extension
items.statement: Assume AC. In the normalized BDI convention $q=1,d=1$, the strong group is $KO^0(\mathrm{pt})=\mathbb Z$. The finite matrices below give gapped one-parameter Dirac Hamiltonians $H_B(k)$, $k\in\mathbb R$, and integer-labelled difference systems with every invariant $\nu\in\mathbb Z$. In particular a single negative mass against the positive reference is the generator. An integer invariant is constant along a continuous gapped path; the integer-labelled systems are not asserted to form a continuous path of changing index.

items.title: Strong, weak, and interaction-stability scope
items.statement:
## Remarks

The A-page table concerns strong invariants of the finite-dimensional stable Dirac-mass extension problem. Weak invariants require additional lattice or torus hypotheses, and the free-fermion table does not assert general interaction stability or a classification of every disordered system.

Proof scope: only the finite-dimensional stable free Dirac-mass model specified on the A page is in scope. The item makes no theorem claim about weak lattice invariants, disordered Hamiltonians, or interacting systems.
